query: I'm evaluating a 79‑year‑old man. Among male ICU patients aged 74–84 admitted with upper GI bleeding, using first ICU stay, stratify first‑72‑hour diagnostic intensity into quartiles and report mean procedure count, mean hospital LOS (days), and in‑hospital mortality per quartile.
final_sql: SELECT p.gender, i.intime, i.los, d.icd_code, COUNT(p.subject_id) AS patient_count, SUM(i.los) / COUNT(p.subject_id) AS avg_los, cume_dist() OVER (PARTITION BY d.icd_code ORDER BY i.intime) AS quartile FROM patients p JOIN icustays i ON p.subject_id = i.subject_id JOIN diagnoses_icd d ON i.hadm_id = d.hadm_id WHERE p.gender = 'M' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM i.intime) BETWEEN 2019 AND 2020 AND d.icd_code IN ('G418', 'G419') AND i.first_careunit = 'ICU' AND i.hadm_id IN (SELECT hadm_id FROM admissions WHERE admission_type = 'UPPER GI BLEEDING') AND i.intime <= i.dischtime + interval '72 hours' GROUP BY p.gender, i.intime, i.los, d.icd_code, quartile ORDER BY quartile, patient_count NULLS LAST;
